glossary.definition: The regions of the 1080x1920 reel canvas the platform UI covers — roughly 108-220 px at top (camera/audio UI), ~320 px at bottom (caption, audio attribution, profile/follow), ~60 px left and ~110-120 px right (like/comment/share/save stack) — leaving a usable center of about 900x1400-1500 px. Multiple 2025-2026 guides converge on these ranges but disagree in exact pixels; no official Meta pixel spec was fetchable [FACT/excerpt on the ranges; exact values ESTIMATE; official numbers UNKNOWN].

The survival test for cover art: covers are cropped differently in feed, profile grid and Explore, so the hook imagery and any text must sit inside the center square of the 1080x1920 cover to survive every crop [FACT/excerpt — reel-cover guides].

The cover poses an unresolved visual question — mid-action, mid-reveal, gaze off-frame toward something unseen — rather than summarizing the reel; in the luxury genre the question is usually access: 'where is this? who lives like this?' [ESTIMATE — synthesis of thumbnail psychology, medium-high confidence].

The property that a profile grid reads as one brand: a repeatable cover template (same type placement, same grade, same margin logic) is the standard mechanism [FACT/excerpt]; for a luxury account this extends to one serif system, generous negative space and a deliberate persona/place/detail cadence [ESTIMATE — brand-design craft].

Instagram's native experiment mechanism (announced Dec 10, 2024): a reel is shown to NON-followers first, ~24 h of views/likes/comments/shares follow, then manual or performance-triggered share to followers; available to public accounts with at least 1,000 followers. Instagram-reported figures (40% of triers post more, 80% of those see increased non-follower reach) are held one notch down because the official announcement page 403-blocked [FACT/excerpt via secondary writeups].

The nine-axis card the director loop applies to every generated still/clip frame before it enters the timeline: exposure*, composition, color harmony, sharpness distribution*, subject separation, physics/realism*, emotional read, continuity fit, genre fit — each 0-2, gate at total >= 12/18 AND no zero on a starred axis [ESTIMATE — weights designed from cited craft, to be calibrated against real batches].

A rubric axis (exposure, sharpness distribution, physics/realism) where a zero forces automatic regeneration regardless of the total score, because each failure is irrecoverable in post: clipped data cannot be un-clipped, AI-tell texture cannot be re-rendered, broken physics cannot be masked [ESTIMATE — triage design, high confidence].

Generation conditioned on two uploaded images so the model produces the motion between them — 'Start & End Frames' on Kling, 'Keyframes' on Runway Gen-3 and Luma; submitting the SAME image as both ends yields a natural loop [FACT/excerpt — Kling/Runway docs excerpts]. Which Higgsfield MCP models expose this parameter is [UNKNOWN here] — owned by the MCP-surface file.

The check that the two frames either side of each cut sit within a tight luminance/hue window with skin on the same target values; adapted from professional Resolve shot-matching practice (waveform for luminance, RGB parade for white balance, vectorscope for skin) and doubling as the transition-plan match check [FACT/excerpt on the base method; adaptation ESTIMATE].

The everything-in-focus look AI frames often carry: no depth hierarchy, every plane equally crisp, which reads synthetic; the rubric requires the sharpest point to be the intended subject (usually the eyes) with the background softer, and flags AI mush zones (hands, text, patterns) as the inverse failure [FACT/excerpt that uniform/warped detail reads AI; the distribution rule ESTIMATE].

nodes.definition: Fix the palette every cover and every rubric color judgment reads against. The classic-luxury brief maps to the warm, muted, timeless 'old money' palette — cream, beige, camel, navy, sage, taupe, tobacco; nothing neon; warm practical light (~2700-3000 K look) reads richer than cool [FACT/excerpt — old-money-aesthetic style guides; the mapping of palette to grade controls is ESTIMATE]. The grade translation [ESTIMATE — colorist craft, medium-high confidence]: skin warm-natural, shadows drifted only slightly cool, global chroma ~10-20% below default, highlights rolled off rather than clipped — muted highlights being the strongest single 'expensive film' cue — and a gentle S-curve with lifted-but-not-milky blacks. This is deliberately NOT full blockbuster teal-orange; the complementary warm-skin-vs-cool-field mechanism is used at a whisper, not a wall. Fitness-accent posts may push slightly more contrast/saturation but stay inside the same palette family so the grid remains coherent.

A cover that only communicates at full size is a failed cover regardless of how beautiful the frame is, because the grid and Explore render it small first.

nodes.definition: Design what the cover SAYS: it should pose an unresolved visual question rather than summarize the reel — mid-action, mid-reveal, a gaze off-frame toward something unseen [ESTIMATE — synthesis of thumbnail psychology, medium-high confidence]. nodes.definition: Design each END(i)/START(i+1) pair by the transition it must serve [ESTIMATE — operationalization of transition craft plus match-cut definition, medium-high confidence; the match-cut definition itself is FACT/excerpt]. whether a scrubbed frame suffices or a designed upload is needed depends on whether the frame passes the legibility test as-is
the grid template's one-grade rule is the house palette applied across all cover frames
the template's margin and type-placement logic must be designed inside the crop-surviving square
a deliberate cover choice must exist and be recorded before any trial's result can be interpreted against it
the observational method exists precisely because trials test the whole reel and offer no cover isolation
holding the template constant is what makes a one-variable cover comparison readable
the exposure checks are scored inside the 0-2 scheme and carry the gate's starred veto
composition is one of the nine axes and inherits the gate's scoring scheme
color harmony is scored 0-2 within the gate's card
the axis tests palette membership against the house family the palette node defines
sharpness distribution is a starred axis of the gate and carries its regeneration veto
subject separation is one of the nine scored axes
the hue-contrast separation mechanism must operate at the restrained whisper the house palette allows
physics/realism is a starred axis whose zero triggers the gate's automatic regeneration
the emotional/continuity/genre reads are the gate's three interpretive axes
the emotional-read axis scores expression legibility at thumbnail size, the same test the face-cover findings established
the chain's stills-fail-cheap economics only work because the rubric gates each still before video generation
the per-transition recipes design the END/START pairs the chain plan calls for
the eye-trace handoff and screen-position matching in the pairing recipes consume the composition axis's placement reads
the same-image loop is the chain's special case where the reel's last end frame equals its first start frame
the QC window verifies the designed pairs and the delivered clips actually match at every cut
the boundary window's hue and skin checks reuse the color axis's vectorscope discipline at cut resolution
the boundary window's luminance check reuses the exposure axis's waveform discipline across the cut
the verdict ranks surviving candidates by the curiosity question they pose
the cadence slot and template fit are the verdict's tie-breakers
accumulated A/B learnings reweight the verdict's rankers, and the verdict's log feeds the next comparisons
a cover candidate must pass the rubric including the emotional/genre reads before it enters the verdict
withholding information for intrigue pulls against instant small-size legibility — the most curious frame is often the least parseable
edges.resolution_rule: readability wins: a curiosity device that cannot be parsed at ~150 px is noise, so the question must be posed with large, legible elements or a different frame is chosen

edges.why_related: face covers out-click other types, but a grid of nine consecutive faces breaks the persona/place/detail cadence the luxury brand needs
edges.resolution_rule: the cadence wins at grid level: face covers take the cadence's persona slots and the highest-stakes reels, rather than every slot

edges.why_related: boundary frames must MATCH on shape and screen position while adjacent shots must DIFFER meaningfully in size or angle to avoid jump cuts
edges.resolution_rule: satisfy both by splitting the variables: match shape and screen position across the cut while jumping shot size (close to wide), which reads as a match cut, not a jump cut

edges.why_related: a frame can clear the 12/18 total while carrying a physics zero — the total-score logic and the starred veto disagree about it
edges.resolution_rule: the starred veto always wins: any zero on exposure, sharpness distribution or physics regenerates the frame regardless of the total, because those failures are irrecoverable in post

edges.why_related: the native trial mechanism cannot isolate the cover variable, while the observational method is confounded but cover-specific — each is tempted to answer the other's question
edges.resolution_rule: route by question: reel-level verdicts (hook, pacing, format) go to Trial Reels; cover-level learnings come only from one-variable observational comparisons, and neither read is quoted as the other

edges.why_related: the big-central-elements rule must operate inside the ~900x1400-1500 px usable center — legible text in a UI-covered margin is still lost
center-square survival is a hard eliminator in the verdict — no candidate that loses its hook or face to a crop may be ranked
accumulated cover comparisons feed back into the template — cadence proportions and type policy are retuned by what the grid data shows

conflict_axes.name: curiosity_gap_vs_thumbnail_clarity
conflict_axes.description: A cover that withholds for intrigue pulls against the requirement that the cover parse instantly at ~150 px; maximal mystery and maximal legibility cannot both be maximized.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: legibility is the floor, curiosity the ceiling: pose the question with large legible elements, and discard curiosity devices that cost the one-second parse

conflict_axes.name: luxury_restraint_vs_clickbait_loudness
conflict_axes.description: Bold text, shock expressions and saturated punch raise raw thumbnail salience, but in the classic-luxury genre restraint IS the click driver and loudness reads new-money.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stay inside the house register — poised intrigue, muted highlights, 3-5 quiet bold words — and let coherence do the clicking; loudness is reserved for nothing

conflict_axes.name: face_ctr_vs_grid_cadence
conflict_axes.description: Faces out-click faceless covers, but a coherent luxury grid needs its persona/place/detail alternation, so the best-clicking cover type cannot fill every slot.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: faces take the persona slots and the highest-stakes reels; place and detail covers hold their cadence slots even when a face frame scores higher individually

conflict_axes.name: designed_polish_vs_feed_native_frame
conflict_axes.description: A designed uploaded cover states the reel's content and controls type, but drifts the grid toward ad-like polish; a scrubbed real frame is feed-native and honest but cedes typographic control.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to a selected real frame passed through the rubric; reserve designed uploads for covers that need type, and even then build them on a real frame from the reel

conflict_axes.name: whole_reel_trial_vs_cover_isolation
conflict_axes.description: Trial Reels give a clean non-follower read of the whole reel but cannot isolate the cover; observational cover comparisons isolate the variable but are confounded by content and timing.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use each for its question — trials for hook/format verdicts, one-variable observational comparisons for covers — and never attribute a trial outcome to the cover

conflict_axes.name: starred_veto_vs_total_score
conflict_axes.description: The rubric's 12/18 total and its starred-zero veto can disagree: a frame can total high while carrying one irrecoverable failure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the veto is absolute — clipped data, AI-tell texture and broken physics cannot be fixed in post, so no total buys a starred zero through the gate

conflict_axes.name: boundary_match_vs_shot_variety
conflict_axes.description: Cut boundaries want the two frames as similar as possible (position, luminance, vector) while sequence grammar wants adjacent shots meaningfully different in size or angle.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split the variables: match shape, screen position, vector and the luminance/hue window at the boundary while jumping shot size and angle — the match-cut recipe satisfies both masters

conflict_axes.name: rubric_strictness_vs_generation_budget
conflict_axes.description: A tight gate protects the account's no-AI-look requirement but each regeneration costs credits and time; a loose gate ships cheaper but risks the credibility the account lives on.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the starred veto absolutely, and spend the budget where failure is cheap — regenerate stills freely before video, and calibrate the 12/18 threshold against real batch costs rather than loosening the starred rows

conflict_axes.name: published_guide_pixels_vs_official_unknown
conflict_axes.description: Safe-zone guides converge on ranges but disagree in exact pixels, and Meta's official numbers were unfetchable; composing to the tightest union wastes canvas while trusting one guide risks covered content.
poles: trust a single guide's tighter numbers
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compose to the conservative union while the official spec is UNKNOWN, and treat any published reel showing UI overlap as immediate evidence to widen the assumed zones

edge_cases.description: The safe-zone guides disagree materially (108 vs 220 px top margin) and no official Meta pixel spec is fetchable, so any single number is unverifiable
edge_cases.trigger: a layout decision needs an exact top-margin pixel value
edge_cases.mitigation: compose to the conservative union of the published ranges, carry the [UNKNOWN] for Meta's official numbers, and re-derive when an official spec or an observed-overlap incident arrives

edge_cases.description: Cover text placed in the bottom 320 px is covered by the caption and audio-attribution UI on published reels
edge_cases.trigger: type is laid out on the full canvas without the safe-zone map
edge_cases.mitigation: keep captions and cover text in the upper-middle center band, never the bottom 320 px or right ~120 px

edge_cases.description: The grid crop beheads the persona because the face sat in the top quarter of the 9:16 frame
edge_cases.trigger: a cover approved on the full-frame view without rendering the center-square and 4:5 crops
edge_cases.mitigation: place faces in the middle 50% vertically and render every candidate in all crop forms before approval

edge_cases.description: A cover reads beautifully at full size but dies at ~150 px grid width because its title is thin serif at five-plus words
edge_cases.trigger: cover review happens only on a desktop full-size preview
edge_cases.mitigation: run the 150 px render test on dark and light backgrounds as a mandatory eliminator before any ranking

edge_cases.description: The '~25% higher CTR for expressive faces' figure is presented as a platform statistic in a strategy document
edge_cases.trigger: the aggregator number is quoted without its [ESTIMATE, medium-low confidence] tag
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the tag in every restatement; the defensible claim is directional (faces out-click, expressive beats neutral), not the number

edge_cases.description: The Trial Reels statistics (40% post more, 80% increased reach) are cited as directly verified official figures although the announcement page 403-blocked
edge_cases.trigger: trial mechanics are documented without the one-notch-down sourcing caveat
edge_cases.mitigation: quote the figures only as secondary-writeup reproductions of an unfetchable official page, and re-verify when creators.instagram.com becomes reachable

edge_cases.description: The account is private or under 1,000 followers, so the planned Trial Reels lane does not exist yet, and the per-account analytics breakdowns are unknown until the account is live
edge_cases.trigger: an A/B plan assumes trial eligibility or specific analytics views before the account qualifies
edge_cases.mitigation: run observational cover comparisons from day one (they need no eligibility), carry the [UNKNOWN until the account exists] on analytics breakdowns, and add trials when the threshold is crossed

edge_cases.description: A uniformly sharp AI frame passes a casual review because nothing is blurry — the failure is the absence of a focus hierarchy, which reads synthetic
edge_cases.trigger: sharpness is scored as present/absent instead of as a distribution
edge_cases.mitigation: score WHERE the sharpest point is and require the background softer than the subject; uniform sharpness is a starred zero, not a pass

edge_cases.description: Two frames each pass the rubric individually but sit outside the luminance/hue window at their shared cut, producing a visible batch seam
edge_cases.trigger: per-frame scoring is treated as sufficient and the pairwise boundary check is skipped
edge_cases.mitigation: run the boundary window on every pair before video generation and again at conform — frame quality is per-frame, cut quality is pairwise

edge_cases.description: The loop plan assumes same-image start/end conditioning but whether any connected Higgsfield model exposes it is unknown, and the fallback dissolve changes the reel's ending
edge_cases.trigger: a loop reel is committed before the MCP-surface capability is confirmed
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the [UNKNOWN here — MCP-surface file] on the capability, design loop reels so the editorial fallback (duplicate first second plus 0.5-1 s dissolve) is acceptable, and confirm before scaling the format

edge_cases.description: The physics axis is scored against an artifact taxonomy this KB does not own — the prompting/QC file's taxonomy has not landed, so the checklist may have gaps
edge_cases.trigger: a physics score is treated as exhaustive while the cross-file taxonomy is still [UNKNOWN here]
edge_cases.mitigation: score with the four named checks (shadows, reflections, motion blur, cloth/hair/liquid), carry the cross-file UNKNOWN, and expand the checklist the moment the taxonomy lands

edge_cases.description: A cover's contrast works in dark mode but the pale title vanishes against the light-mode app background (or vice versa)
edge_cases.trigger: contrast is checked in only one app theme
edge_cases.mitigation: render the 150 px test on both dark and light backgrounds and require the candidate to pass both before ranking

workflow.action: Fix the canvas and safe-zone map
workflow.description: State 9:16 1080x1920, the four margin ranges with their ESTIMATE tag and the official-spec UNKNOWN, and adopt the conservative-union rule
workflow.gate: the map carries the ranges, the usable-center estimate, both honesty tags and the conservative-union rule

workflow.description: Require hook imagery, text and faces to survive the feed, grid and Explore crops, with faces in the middle 50% vertically
workflow.gate: every cover candidate is rendered in the center-square and 4:5 crops before approval

workflow.description: Name the old-money hue family, muted-highlight and mild-desaturation rules, and the in-family fitness-accent allowance
workflow.gate: the palette names its hue family, highlight policy and variance allowance with sources tagged

workflow.action: Stand up the nine-axis rubric gate
workflow.description: Define the 0-2 axes, the >=12/18 total, the starred veto on exposure/sharpness/physics, and the calibrate-later tag on weights
workflow.gate: the card lists all nine axes, the threshold, the starred set and the ESTIMATE tag on weights

workflow.action: Score every generated frame on the starred hard axes
workflow.description: Run waveform exposure, sharpness-distribution and physics checks at full zoom and playback; any zero regenerates
workflow.gate: no frame with a starred zero proceeds; scores are logged for calibration

workflow.action: Score the compositional and interpretive axes
workflow.description: Score composition, color harmony, subject separation, emotional read, continuity fit and genre fit against the house targets
workflow.gate: each admitted frame totals >=12/18 with all notes recorded

workflow.action: Design the reel as a chain of boundary stills with per-transition pairs
workflow.description: For each cut choose the transition, design END(i)/START(i+1) by its recipe (match cut, whip, occlusion, loop), and regenerate failing stills before any video
workflow.gate: every pair names its recipe and both stills passed the rubric before video generation

workflow.action: Run boundary QC on pairs and delivered clips
workflow.description: Check every cut's two frames inside the luminance/hue window on scopes with shared skin targets, pre-generation and at conform
workflow.gate: all cut boundaries pass the scoped window twice

workflow.action: Construct the loop where the reel calls for one
workflow.description: Use same-image conditioning if the surface supports it (UNKNOWN until confirmed) or the frame-match/dissolve fallback, and loop the caption sentence across the restart
workflow.gate: the zoomed first/last frame check passes and the sentence reads across the restart

workflow.action: Select the cover through the ranked verdict
workflow.description: Eliminate on crop/safe-zone/legibility, rank on face and curiosity, tie-break on cadence, and log the cover's variables
workflow.gate: the published cover passed the eliminators in order and its variables are logged

workflow.action: Assemble the grid against the template
workflow.description: Place the cover in its cadence slot and confirm the nine-tile mock still reads as one system with both personas distinguishable
workflow.gate: the updated grid mock holds one grade, one type system and the cadence

workflow.description: Compare matched posts varying one cover variable, read grid-sourced views when the account's analytics surface is known, and feed learnings back to the verdict and template
workflow.gate: each comparison varied one variable across multiple posts per variant and its conclusion is logged

dominance_rules.rule: The grounding file's honesty tag dominates any pixel value, engagement figure or capability claim
dominance_rules.rationale: every cited page 403-blocked this session, so [FACT/excerpt] claims sit one notch below FACT, aggregator numbers are ESTIMATE, and Higgsfield capabilities are UNKNOWN here — restating any of them stronger fabricates
dominance_rules.trigger: a safe-zone pixel, CTR figure, trial statistic or model capability is about to be stated
dominance_rules.action: quote it at exactly the tag the research carries, name the blocker for UNKNOWNs, and never invent a Meta spec or Higgsfield parameter

dominance_rules.rule: The starred-axis veto dominates the rubric total
dominance_rules.rationale: clipped data, AI-tell texture and broken physics are irrecoverable in post, so no aggregate score can buy them through
dominance_rules.trigger: a frame totals >=12/18 while carrying a zero on exposure, sharpness distribution or physics
dominance_rules.action: regenerate the frame; the total is never consulted when a starred row is zero

dominance_rules.rule: Crop and safe-zone survival dominate compositional beauty for covers
dominance_rules.rationale: a cover is consumed in its cropped, UI-overlaid forms, so content the crop or overlay removes does not exist for the viewer
dominance_rules.trigger: a candidate scores highest on composition but loses its hook, text or face in the center-square, 4:5 or safe-zone render
dominance_rules.action: eliminate the candidate before ranking; only crop-surviving frames compete on beauty

dominance_rules.rule: Thumbnail legibility dominates the curiosity gap
dominance_rules.rationale: an unparseable mystery is indistinguishable from noise at 150 px, so the question must be legible to work at all
dominance_rules.trigger: a curiosity device (occlusion, withheld subject, off-frame gaze) costs the one-second parse at grid size
dominance_rules.action: re-pose the question with larger legible elements or choose a different frame

dominance_rules.rule: Grid restraint dominates single-cover click optimization
dominance_rules.rationale: in the classic-luxury genre coherence and restraint carry the positioning that earns clicks over time, and loud covers spend brand for one post's CTR
dominance_rules.trigger: a loud, text-heavy or shock-expression cover outscores the in-register alternative on projected salience
dominance_rules.action: publish the in-register cover in its cadence slot and log the forgone variant for observational comparison

dominance_rules.rule: Pairwise boundary matching dominates per-frame excellence at cut points
dominance_rules.rationale: viewers see cuts, not frames — two individually perfect frames that mismatch in luminance, hue or vector read as a batch seam
dominance_rules.trigger: a frame pair passes per-frame scoring but fails the boundary window or vector match
dominance_rules.action: regenerate or re-pair the boundary stills before video generation rather than admitting the seam

dominance_rules.rule: Regenerating stills dominates fixing in post, and stills-stage failure dominates video-stage failure
dominance_rules.rationale: stills are cheaper than video as a category on credit platforms, and post can add blur or trims but cannot author detail, physics or clipped data
dominance_rules.trigger: a flawed still is about to be carried into video generation on the hope of a timeline rescue
dominance_rules.action: fail it now: regenerate the still until the rubric passes, then spend video credits

dominance_rules.rule: One-variable observational discipline dominates multi-variable cover experimentation
dominance_rules.rationale: with no native cover A/B, confounded comparisons are the only lane — varying two things at once destroys even that
dominance_rules.trigger: a new cover changes face/detail AND text policy AND question type against its comparison set
dominance_rules.action: hold all but one variable to the template and log the varied one at publish time

dominance_rules.rule: The closed likeness lane dominates any engagement upside
dominance_rules.rationale: the repo honesty contract keeps guidance for evoking a specific real person while hiding the face out of scope entirely
dominance_rules.trigger: a cover or frame concept drifts toward a recognizable real individual's likeness
dominance_rules.action: refuse the direction and redesign with the account's own personas

anti_rework_rules.rule: Rubric-pass every START and END still before generating any video between them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: paying video-generation prices to discover a failure that was visible in a cheap still

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design the END(i)/START(i+1) pair per its transition recipe before generating either clip
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating whole clips because two independently designed boundaries share no shape, vector or occlusion state to cut on

anti_rework_rules.rule: Render every cover candidate at ~150 px in both app modes and in the center-square and 4:5 crops before approval
anti_rework_rules.prevents: republishing or living with a cover whose text or face dies in the grid after the reel is already live

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep all cover text and captions out of the bottom 320 px and right ~120 px from the first layout pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-laying-out and re-exporting reels whose type the caption bar and button stack cover

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock the house palette and grid template before producing any covers
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regrading and recomposing an entire grid of covers when a late template decision changes the type placement or grade

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm start/end-frame and loop support on the connected Higgsfield surface before committing a loop-format series
anti_rework_rules.prevents: replanning a whole series when the assumed same-image loop mode turns out not to exist on the available models

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the boundary luminance/hue window on still pairs before generation, not only on delivered clips at conform
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering batch color seams after video credits are spent, when the fix is regenerating clips instead of stills

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log every published cover's variables (face/detail, text/none, designed/scrubbed, question type) at publish time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing cover history from memory when enough posts exist to read comparisons, and losing months of implicit experiments

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first real generation batches arrive with rubric scores logged
iteration_protocol.action: calibrate the 12/18 threshold, the axis weights and the boundary-window width against observed regeneration cost and shipped quality

iteration_protocol.trigger: the MCP-surface file lands which Higgsfield models expose start/end-frame conditioning, fps and credit prices
iteration_protocol.action: resolve the capability UNKNOWNs, recompute the stills-first economics, and commit or drop the same-image loop format

iteration_protocol.trigger: an official Meta safe-zone or cover-crop spec becomes fetchable, or a published reel shows UI covering assumed-safe content
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimated margin ranges with the verified values (or widen the conservative union) and re-audit existing templates

iteration_protocol.trigger: the account goes live and its real analytics breakdowns become visible
iteration_protocol.action: replace the assumed observational read with the actual grid-sourced metrics and start the cover A/B ledger against them

iteration_protocol.trigger: accumulated cover comparisons reach multiple posts per variant on a question
iteration_protocol.action: update the verdict's ranker weights and the grid cadence proportions with the observed winners

iteration_protocol.trigger: the prompting/QC file's AI-artifact taxonomy lands
iteration_protocol.action: expand the physics and sharpness checklists from the taxonomy and re-score any frames admitted under the four-check interim

iteration_protocol.trigger: a generation model update shifts its color signature, tone mapping or depth-of-field rendering
iteration_protocol.action: re-baseline the color-harmony, exposure and sharpness checks and re-verify the boundary window on the next batch

priority_rationale: The canvas facts come first (safe zones, center-square crop, house palette) because every cover and frame judgment is made inside them; the rubric gate and its axes come next because nothing enters a timeline or a cover shortlist without passing them; the frame-chain nodes (start/end chain, pairing rules, loop, boundary QC) build on the rubric because their whole economics is failing frames cheaply before video; and the cover-selection stack (readability, face, curiosity, source, grid, A/B, verdict) closes because it composes everything upstream into the account's single highest-leverage published choice.
